items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: and a drummer named Monk McVey (Nathaniel McVey, who was playing the drums)

ctx.x: Oh yeah, because I was in the idiom more or less to my liking and my desires. Roy Milton I appreciated was beautiful, you know. But Howard McGhee, they were playing more advanced music, you know. And I'm a youngster. I'm eager to play with something more advanced. Like, we were the counterparts to Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie; they were on the East Coast and we were out here, you know, when we put our thing together.

So we put the group together. We had Stanley Morgan playing the guitar, and a very fine pianist, Vernon Biddle, playing the piano, and a drummer named Monk McVey (Nathaniel McVey, who was playing the drums), and Bob Kesterson(?) was the bassist. And we had rehearsed and worked on the music and everything, and... Our first job with the band was the Downbeat Club on 42nd and Central.
